source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. A misty fen and its town of seven bell towers, where children vanish on foggy nights and folk whisper of a mist witch: grey water, reeds, lanterns blurred by fog, far bells answering each other across the marsh. Misty, melancholy and mysterious, but with the warmth of the townsfolk; a lilting, singable 6/8 folk ballad. Tempo 92 BPM, 6/8 time, key of E dorian. Instrumentation: low whistle melody, fiddle answer, celtic harp, soft bodhran, cello drone, distant tuned church bells, a little accordion. Form: harp and bell pickup; section A low whistle melody; section B fiddle melody, a little darker; a quiet interlude with distant bells; section A again with fuller band. Duration: 90 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
